snapshot.comment:
Qualified user-approved CLIC polymer candidate only; not a measured industrial recipe, commercial-grade equivalence or scientific certification. Existing lifetime purchases and all unrelated exchanges are preserved. Automatic propagation does not authorize changes to protected PV dependency closures.

Native3.12 emulsion-route dry PTFE is an upstream resin-production burden proxy for granular molding stock, NOT a verified interchangeable granular compression grade. Select unfilled, non-expanded compression/sinter/skive/cut forming, not ordinary melt injection. Assume95% forming/cutting retention, with3 MJ heat and0.2 kWh/kg finished as engineering allowances. Native polymerization yields/burdens are embedded upstream. Remove local monomer and7.5 MJ/0.5 kWh polymerization allowances. Retain the existing solid-reject proxy without a new native-service residual, filler, processing aid, emission or credit. Finished-gasket EOL is owned by the unchanged stack-treatment inventory. Only3.12 target compatibility is proposed; no latest3.9 promise.

snapshot.name: polytetrafluoroethylene gasket production, forming, resin supply proxy
snapshot.source: Independent foreground forming reference for 1 kg of unfilled PTFE gasket. Purchases 1/0.95 kg of native ecoinvent 3.12 PTFE resin as a production-burden proxy; the native emulsion-route resin is not a verified granular moulding grade. The approved 95% forming/cutting retention, 3 MJ heat and 0.2 kWh electricity per kg finished are explicit engineering assumptions, not supplier measurements. Manufacturing reject is 1/0.95 - 1 kg, assigned to the existing generic waste-plastic outlet as an imperfect burden proxy; no recovery credit or validated fluoropolymer abatement is claimed. Resin polymerisation burdens remain embedded in the external supplier: no separate local monomer, 7.5 MJ heat or 0.5 kWh electricity purchase is present. Finished-gasket disposal remains with the existing stack-treatment inventory. Chemours granular PTFE processing guidance and Daikin M/F-series product descriptions support the forming-route distinction, not these numerical allowances. Gerloff 2021 (10.1016/j.est.2021.102759) and the Power-to-Methane SI (10.1021/acssuschemeng.1c02002.s001, page S12) provide application context and the separately retained 144.2 kg stack purchase; that purchase is not a coefficient of this per-kg forming recipe. The PtM SI is CC BY-NC 4.0; this foreground designation does not relicense that SI or decide the rights in the consumer inventory. Hintzer et al., Fluoropolymers (10.1002/14356007.a11_393.pub2), is historical property/process context. CC BY 4.0 covers only the compiler's rights in the original foreground compilation, subject to authenticated authority; source publications, trademarks and native supplier inventory bodies remain separately licensed.
